### What the session covers

**Part 1 · The idea.** What an agent really is; two agents with two jobs, a
researcher and a reviewer; why keeping them apart removes bias; the three rules
the session lives by (separate, trace, admit doubt); and why the process has to
run in this order.

**Part 2 · The live run.** `/researcher` reads everything and writes an
evidence briefing with no opinions in it. At the human checkpoint you correct
the *evidence*, not the conclusions. `/reviewer` then critiques the briefing
through five lenses, without ever opening the original strategy. A LOW
confidence rating is traced back to its source passage; the evidence is
changed and one step re-run.
:::

::: {}
### How it works

Session 2 used agents to go faster. This one uses them to be more trustworthy.
The reviewer works only from `output/research-briefing.md`, so it cannot
rationalise evidence to fit a conclusion it has already formed. Every finding
cites a file and a passage; a claim that cannot be traced is removed, not
softened. `output/audit-log.md` records every action and source, which is the
part that lets you stand behind the report.
:::
:::

### Replicate it

::: {.steps}
1. Download the zip above and unzip it. Open a terminal in the `03_multitudes` folder.
2. Make sure **Python** and `pip` are available; the final report is written with `python-docx`.
3. Start Claude Code and run the two agents in order:
   ```text
   claude
   /researcher
   /reviewer
   ```
4. Read the briefing at the checkpoint and fix anything the researcher got wrong before running `/reviewer`. The report and audit log land in `output/`.
5. Put your own strategy, its predecessor and a context note in `sample-input/` (or any folder) and run `/strategy-review` for the full pipeline.
:::

The same folder works in Codex via `AGENTS.md`, which keeps the reviewer blind
to the original document in the same way.
